answer.explanation:
Here are the CYP profiles for the two requested compounds from the supplied data and model predictions. The batch remains unchanged.

Concise table (uncalibrated scores; lower is not a clinical claim):
- Aspirin: CYP1A2 0.0010 | CYP2C9 0.0221 | CYP2C19 0.0335 | CYP2D6 0.0136 | CYP3A4 0.0001
- Ibuprofen: CYP1A2 0.0002 | CYP2C9 0.0810 | CYP2C19 0.1277 | CYP2D6 0.0832 | CYP3A4 0.0001

Profile summary:
- Aspirin is predicted highest among the five endpoints at CYP2C19, with CYP2C9 and CYP2D6 also above its CYP3A4 and CYP1A2 scores.
- Ibuprofen is predicted highest at CYP2C19 as well, with CYP2C9 and CYP2D6 next, and very low CYP3A4 and CYP1A2 scores.
- Relative to aspirin, ibuprofen has higher scores on CYP2C9, CYP2C19, and CYP2D6, while CYP3A4 is the same to four decimal places.

If you want, I can also format this as a CSV-style row pair or add the other two compounds already present in the batch for comparison.

papers.title: Preclinical strategy to reduce clinical hepatotoxicity using in vitro bioactivation data for >200 compounds.
papers.authors: Sakatis MZ, Reese MJ, Harrell AW, Taylor MA, Baines IA, Chen L, Bloomer JC, Yang EY, Ellens HM, Ambroso JL, Lovatt CA, Ayrton AD, Clarke SE.
papers.abstract: Drug-induced liver injury is the most common cause of market withdrawal of pharmaceuticals, and thus, there is considerable need for better prediction models for DILI early in drug discovery. We present a study involving 223 marketed drugs (51% associated with clinical hepatotoxicity; 49% non-hepatotoxic) to assess the concordance of in vitro bioactivation data with clinical hepatotoxicity and have used these data to develop a decision tree to help reduce late-stage candidate attrition. Data to assess P450 metabolism-dependent inhibition (MDI) for all common drug-metabolizing P450 enzymes were generated for 179 of these compounds, GSH adduct data generated for 190 compounds, covalent binding data obtained for 53 compounds, and clinical dose data obtained for all compounds. Individual data for all 223 compounds are presented here and interrogated to determine what level of an alert to consider termination of a compound. The analysis showed that 76% of drugs with a daily dose of <100 mg were non-hepatotoxic (p < 0.0001). Drugs with a daily dose of ≥100 mg or with GSH adduct formation, marked P450 MDI, or covalent binding ≥200 pmol eq/mg protein tended to be hepatotoxic (∼ 65% in each case). Combining dose with each bioactivation assay increased this association significantly (80-100%, p < 0.0001). These analyses were then used to develop the decision tree and the tree tested using 196 of the compounds with sufficient data (49% hepatotoxic; 51% non-hepatotoxic). The results of these outcome analyses demonstrated the utility of the tree in selectively terminating hepatotoxic compounds early; 45% of the hepatotoxic compounds evaluated using the tree were recommended for termination before candidate selection, whereas only 10% of the non-hepatotoxic compounds were recommended for termination. An independent set of 10 GSK compounds with known clinical hepatotoxicity status were also assessed using the tree, with similar results.

papers.title: Development of a cell viability assay to assess drug metabolite structure-toxicity relationships.
papers.authors: Rana P, Will Y, Nadanaciva S, Jones LH.
papers.abstract: Many adverse drug reactions are caused by the cytochrome P450 (CYP)-dependent activation of drugs into reactive metabolites. In order to reduce attrition due to metabolism-induced toxicity and to improve the safety of drug candidates, we developed a simple cell viability assay by combining a bioactivation system (human CYP3A4, CYP2D6 and CYP2C9) with Hep3B cells. We screened a series of drugs to explore structural motifs that may be responsible for CYP450-dependent activation caused by reactive metabolite formation, which highlighted specific liabilities regarding certain phenols and anilines.

outcome.explanation: I looked up exact-structure CYP3A4 evidence for aspirin from ChEMBL. The retrieved snapshot shows five activity records total, all at the same exact-structure match (CHEMBL25) and all with no numeric IC50/Ki value reported. Two records are labeled Not Active for the DRUGMATRIX CYP450 3A4 enzyme inhibition assay using 7-Benzyloxy-4-(trifluoromethyl)-coumarin, with the comment that inhibition was <50% at 10 uM so a dose-response curve was not measured. Three other records are labeled Active in separate CYP3A4 inhibition/activation-related assays: two 2012 Chem Res Toxicol assays reporting CYP3A4 inhibition as a ratio involving 7-benzyloxyquinoline or diethoxyfluorescein substrates, and one 2016 Bioorg Med Chem Lett cell-based activation-related assay with FC = 1.0. Caveats: these are different assay questions and substrates, so they should not be pooled as one result; the non-numeric labels do not give a measured potency; and the evidence is retrospective ChEMBL playback, not a fresh experimental readout. The batch was kept unchanged.

papers.title: Preclinical strategy to reduce clinical hepatotoxicity using in vitro bioactivation data for >200 compounds.
papers.authors: Sakatis MZ, Reese MJ, Harrell AW, Taylor MA, Baines IA, Chen L, Bloomer JC, Yang EY, Ellens HM, Ambroso JL, Lovatt CA, Ayrton AD, Clarke SE.
papers.abstract: Drug-induced liver injury is the most common cause of market withdrawal of pharmaceuticals, and thus, there is considerable need for better prediction models for DILI early in drug discovery. We present a study involving 223 marketed drugs (51% associated with clinical hepatotoxicity; 49% non-hepatotoxic) to assess the concordance of in vitro bioactivation data with clinical hepatotoxicity and have used these data to develop a decision tree to help reduce late-stage candidate attrition. Data to assess P450 metabolism-dependent inhibition (MDI) for all common drug-metabolizing P450 enzymes were generated for 179 of these compounds, GSH adduct data generated for 190 compounds, covalent binding data obtained for 53 compounds, and clinical dose data obtained for all compounds. Individual data for all 223 compounds are presented here and interrogated to determine what level of an alert to consider termination of a compound. The analysis showed that 76% of drugs with a daily dose of <100 mg were non-hepatotoxic (p < 0.0001). Drugs with a daily dose of ≥100 mg or with GSH adduct formation, marked P450 MDI, or covalent binding ≥200 pmol eq/mg protein tended to be hepatotoxic (∼ 65% in each case). Combining dose with each bioactivation assay increased this association significantly (80-100%, p < 0.0001). These analyses were then used to develop the decision tree and the tree tested using 196 of the compounds with sufficient data (49% hepatotoxic; 51% non-hepatotoxic). The results of these outcome analyses demonstrated the utility of the tree in selectively terminating hepatotoxic compounds early; 45% of the hepatotoxic compounds evaluated using the tree were recommended for termination before candidate selection, whereas only 10% of the non-hepatotoxic compounds were recommended for termination. An independent set of 10 GSK compounds with known clinical hepatotoxicity status were also assessed using the tree, with similar results.

papers.title: Development of a cell viability assay to assess drug metabolite structure-toxicity relationships.
papers.authors: Rana P, Will Y, Nadanaciva S, Jones LH.
papers.abstract: Many adverse drug reactions are caused by the cytochrome P450 (CYP)-dependent activation of drugs into reactive metabolites. In order to reduce attrition due to metabolism-induced toxicity and to improve the safety of drug candidates, we developed a simple cell viability assay by combining a bioactivation system (human CYP3A4, CYP2D6 and CYP2C9) with Hep3B cells. We screened a series of drugs to explore structural motifs that may be responsible for CYP450-dependent activation caused by reactive metabolite formation, which highlighted specific liabilities regarding certain phenols and anilines.
